MA Malek with Jamiruddin Ahmed Fariduddin Ahmed and M Iman Ali, Advocates -----For the Appellants
MA Latif, Advocate -----For the State.
parties:
Abdul Ali and others ----- Appellant
Vs.
State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Abdul Bari Sarker, J.: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by Mr. MA Rob Mollah, Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court Mymensingh in Sessions Case No. 265 of 1980. 

 2. The prosecution case as given in court by the informant Amal Chandra Singh PW 1 is, that his father Tariny Kanta Singh of village Brahman Khali PS Gafargaon, District Mymensingh was a deed writer at the Kandipara Sub-Registrar's Office and he used to live in his village home and look after his landed properties. He further said that his mother died about 20/25 years ago leaving him as his only son and no other issue. He said that Nikhil Chandra Singh PW 2, his mother Sarja Bala and sister. Bindu came to reside with his father in the same house and they used to look after the household affairs of his father. He further said that he PW 1 left the house in 1964 for prosecution of studies and after passing the M Com. examination, he took a job at Dhaka in the Milk Vita Firm and resides with his wife and minor son at Dhaka. He said that the accused appellants Abdul Ali and Abdul Bari purchased share of his father's co-sharers Gopal Chand Singh and Hori Narayan Singh in the homestead and started living there and for this his father filed a pre-emption case, obtained a decree against them and filed petition for delivery of possession vide the certified copy of order Ext. 6. But in spite of that those appellants were opposing his father's possession in the land and started enmity with him. Besides that the borgader and others became inimical towards his father and were conspiring to grab this property and the reatened him and for fear of life his father left the village 2/3 months prior to the occurrence and came to reside with him at Dhaka. He said that on 22.12.78 his father made a GD Entry vide Ext. 1 in the Gafargaon PS to the effect that his brothers and other interested persons were holding out threat to him. He further said that PW 2 Nikhil and his mother wrote letters vide Exts. 4 and 15 respectively to his wife Anita Rani PW 24 to the effect that they are not in a position to look after their properties any more and his father should go to that village and take over charge of his properties. He said that his father apprised him of the development and accordingly he PW 1 informed OC and SP Mymensingh by two separate petitions Exts. 2 and 3 respectively to the effect that the persons named in the petition were putting out threat to him and his father that they will be killed. He further said that accused Motaleb took forcible possession in one of their lands which formed in Brahmaputra and his father transferred that land to one Fazlur Rahman and others by deed of exchange and Fazlur Rahman and others took possession in that land by evicting accused Motaleb about a year prior to the date of occurrence. He said that Motaleb along with other accused persons being offended started conspiring against his father. He further said that Nikhil and his mother also raised a plea that they kept an amount of Taka 4000.00 and Taka 5000.00 in deposit with his father and demanded that money from his father. They also demanded 8 Kathas of land from his father as price of their service to his father and his father refused to fulfil any of the demands and on that refusal both Nikhil and his mother got angry with his father and the relationship of his father with Nikhil PW 2 and his mother become sore. He further said that about a fortnight before the occurrence Nikhil came to his Dhaka residence and assured his father that none would do any harm to him if he returned to the village home and thus induced his father to return to the village. He further said that accused Abdul Jabbar, Lal Mia, Alam, Kamal, Aziz, Sobhan, Falania had put pressure on his father to part with his landed properties to them on nominal price and leave for India. His father also was having troubles with Borgaders. The above accused persons allegedly threatened his father that if he did not transfer his land to them, they would take forcible possession of his landed properties by forging documents and they would also kill him and the informant. 

 3. He said that on 1.3.79 his father left Dhaka for Mymensingh saying that he would at first make enquiry at Mymensingh and then started for his village home. At that time, the deceased allegedly had given him the list Ext. 8 containing the names of 14 persons who were allegedly making conspiracy against him. PW 1 further said that on 3.5.79, his co-villagers Kartick Chandra Singh PW 19 went to his Dhaka residence and informed him that on the night following 4.3.79 at about 11:00 PM 10/12 persons forcibly entered into the hut of his father and abducted him to an unknown place and Nikhil and his mother informed Kartick about the occurrence. He said that on 6.3.79, he lodged the FIR Ext. 20 at about 6-30 AM with Gafargaon PS. He said that after lodging the FIR, he went to his village home, being accompanied by one police constable of Gafargaon PS, made searches for his father and on 8.3.79 at about dusk time, he got an information that the dead body of his father was found in a doba of Brahmaputra river in the west of village Chartaki under Pakundia police station. He said that the police recovered the dead body of his father from the doba and the dead body was drowned by fastening three bags of sand and bricks. He said that the belly of the dead body was cut and the intestine came out of the belly and there was marks of ink on the left three fingers. He said that the dead body of his father Tariny Kanta Singh was recognised by him and his co-villagers Sunil Kumar Sarker, Taib Ali Member PW 26 and others. He said that the dead body was guarded by police and on the next day Daroga of Pakundia police station came and held inquest on the same, on identification by himself in presence of Sunil and Taib Ali Member and then sent the same to the morgue under police escort. He said that the police visited their house and on 6.3.79 arrested Nikhil, his sister Bindu and their mother. While he was in the village, PW 1 also came to learn that the accused persons took away all the landed properties of his father by forging kabalas and on search at Kuliar Char Sub-Registry office, he obtained the certified copy of the kabala vide Ext. 9 from which it appears that his father allegedly executed the kabala on 26.10.78 in favour of accuseds Abdul Jabbar, Abdus Sobhan and 4(four) others and accused Hafizuddin Sarker wrote that kabala as a scribe. He said that in the meantime the CID took up investigation of the case and recovered the original Kabala Ext. 9 from the office of the Sub-Registry Office. 

 5. PW 34 SI Golam Satter said that he was Officer-in-Charge of Gafargaon police station on 5.3.79 and SI Mr. Kazi Ashraf Ali recorded the FIR Ext. 20 and he himself investigated the case in part. He said that on receipt of a telephone message on 5.3.79 at about 9 AM he went to the house of late Tariny Babu and found PW 2, his mother and sister there. He gave a detailed description of the condition in which he found that house of late Tariny Babu. He said that the informant also went to his house on that date and he prepared the sketch map Ext. 3 of the PO with index Ext. 32. He said that he asked the police to search for Tariny Babu and recover him alive or dead. He said that on the night following 8.3.79, he was informed by police force in the thana over telephone that the dead body of Tariny was recovered from a doba of river Brahmaputra by the side of village Char Taki under Pakundia Police Station and he asked the police to keep watch over the dead body and requested the Officer-in-Charge Pakundia to hold inquest on the dead body. He said that on 9.3.79, he went to the place of occurrence and found that the inquest on the dead body was already held. He said that he seized the three empty gunny bags, three pieces of broken bricks, three jute ropes as per the seizure list Ext. 33. He also seized certain alamats from the house of one Akkas Ali as per the seizure list Ext. 34 on 9.3.79. He said that on 11.3.79 he seized two letters with two envelops and a piece of paper containing names of 4 persons produced by PW 1 as per the seizure list Ext. 35. He also prepared the sketch map Ext. 36 of the place from where the dead body was recovered with the index Ext 37. He said that he arrested FIR named accused Nikhil, his mother Suruja Bala Devi and sister Bindu Bashini. He said, that he examined witnesses and afterwards the investigation of the case was taken up by cm. He said that he got the papers Exts. 3 at the thana. 

 6. PW 36 Sk. Abul Basher said that he was Inspector, CID Mymensingh between April, 1979 to February, 1980 and he took up the investigation of the present case on 14.4.79 at the order of the DIG,  cm and got the papers of the case from the previous Investigating officer Mr. Golam Sabbir. He said that he visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map and on secret information came to learn that the landed properties of deceased Tariny was misappropriated by certain persons by forging deeds and seized the kabala Ext. 9. He also seized one note book petition on plain and deed No. 8772 dated 7.11.75 on 13.7.79 as per seizure list Ext. 39. He also seized some other documents and a register kabala from Kuliarchar Sub-Registrar office. He obtained the signature and thumb impression of certain persons and sent the same to the hand writing expert for examination and on receipt of the report of the hand writing and figure print experts and on examination of witnesses submitted charge sheet against the accused persons. He said that he seized a kabala from the office of the Kuliar Char Sub-Registrar office on 11.6.79 as per the seizure list Ext. 41. 

 8. The accused persons pleaded not guilty to the charge. The defence case appears from the trend of cross-examination of the PWs is, that deceased Tariny Kanta Singh was a man of bad character. He used to sexually enjoy Sarju Bala and Bindu Bashini, the mother and sister respectively of Nikhil Chandra PW 2 and some other women. He might be killed by somebody else and the dead body recovered by the police and PW I was not the dead body of Tariny Kanta Singh. 

 9. The accused persons have been falsely implicated in this case out of enmity and grudge. 

 11. Mr. MA Khalek, the learned Advocate for the appellants has taken us through the FIR, the depositions of the witnesses, the impugned judgment and order, materials on record. He submits that PW 2 Nikhil Chandra Singh who was examined as an approver in the case, is the only witness to allege the involvements of the appellants in the alleged murder of Tariny and there is no other evidence to show their involvement. He submits that the evidence of an approver cannot be a basis for conviction in a case like this without corroborative evidence and in the present case there is no such corroborative evidence. The learned Advocate further submits that appellant Abdus Sobhan died while he was in confinement in jail but there is no papers to show whether the accused appellant Sobhan is really dead or not. 

 12. In only view of the matter let us see what evidence the prosecution adduced to prove its case. 

 13. In the present case as said by the learned Advocate for the appellants, PW 2 Nikhil Chandra Singh is the main witness or rather the only witness of the prosecution to prove its case. 

 15. PW 2 said that he is a resident of Brahmakhali under Gafargaon police station and late Tariny Kanta Singh was their neighbour, residing in the same homestead. He said that his father Sudhir Chandra Singh died while he was aged about two and half years leaving himself as a son, his mother Surja Bala and sister Bindu Bala and they were brought up by Tariny Kanata Singh who used to maintain them after the death of his father. He said that his sister was given in marriage by Tariny at his own expenses with one Sudhir Chandra Singh and after the death of Sudhir she was again given in marriage by Tariny with Kartick Chandra Singh PW 19, of Tangabo village under Gafargaon PS. He said that Tariny gave him education and he passed the SSC Examination in 1974 from Bashia High School. He said that the house of his father is at a distance of 500/600 cubits to the east of the house of Tariny. He said that he sold his paternal properties at Taka 4500.00 and cattles and kept a total of Taka 4807.00 in deposit with Tariny. He said that he sold his paternal homestead and land to accused Abdul Jabbar and others. He further said that he himself, his mother and sister used to reside in the same but with Tariny who had only one dwelling but in his house. He said that appellant Abdul Ali purchased the share of one Hari Kanta Singh and co-sharer of Tariny in the homestead and accused appellant Abdul Bari purchased the share of one Gopal Chandra Singh in that very homestead about 7/8 years before the occurrence and they had quarrel regarding the boundary of the homestead with Tariny who filed a pre-emption case against them. He denied the suggession that there was no such quarrel. 

 18. In cross-examination, PW 2 said that he was confined at hajat at Mymensingh for one and half year and PW 1 did not meet him during that period. He said that his mother and sister were released from hajat 6/7 months after their arrest. He said that before his confessional statement before Magistrate, he made another confessional statement before Mr. Basher, CID Inspector PW 36. He said that he sent an application vide Ext. A to the Magistrate through the Jail authority stating that he will confess. He denied the suggestion that he made that application at the instance of Mr. Bashir PW 36 and made the confessional statement at his instance on the understanding that his sister and mother would be released. He said that he was arrested on 6.3.79 and he made statement to Gafargaon police station on 8.3.79 but on that date, he did not disclose to the police the facts which he stated above in court, regarding the involvement of the accused persons with the abduction and murder of the deceased. He said that he was taken to Magistrate on 20.3.79 but he declined to confess on that date, as the accused persons threatened him and he stated to the Magistrate that he would not confess. He said that accused Abdus Sobhan, Lal Miah and others were holding out threats. He said that he became repentant soon after the occurrence and arrest. But he could not confess for fear of the accused persons. He said that on 20.3.79, he told the Magistrate that he did not know anything. He said that the accused persons did not break any lock and they took only a leather bag and a torch light. He admitted that Jagadish Charan and Ajit are his paternal uncles and they left for Assam after selling their lands to accused Quddus. He denied the suggestion that he killed the young calf of accused Abdul Bari as it damaged his crops and there was a salish and he was fined Taka 100.00 for that. He also denied the suggestion that Atar Ali, son of accused Abdul Ali threw dust at his mother, when she went to fetch water from a tank and there was a quarrel over the matter with Mar Ali. He also denied the suggestion that he was assaulted by accused Motaleb Khan in a quarrel over football game. He said that on the following day after the occurrence, police of Gafargaon PS came to their house on being informed by Umed Ali Master PW 6 over phone and questioned him as to how the occurrence took place and he told them that the dacoits abducted TarinyBabu by putting gamcha on his mouth and at that time he did not state to the police what the accused persons taught him to say. He admitted that he cannot mention the particular dates on which the accused persons had talk with him and induced him to co-operate with them in the matter of abduction and murder of Tariny. He said that he told the daroga on query as to how the door of Tariny's house was opened on the night of the occurrence, that he went out of the house to answer the call of nature by keeping the door open and during that period the miscreants entered into the hut through the open door. He said that there was the hurricane burning inside the hut and he told the daroga about the occurrence. He said that the wife of Tariny Kanta Singha died about 17/18 years before the occurrence. He denied the suggestion that Tariny used to treat his mother and sister as his concubines and slept with them in the same bed and he could not tolerate that relationship as son and brother and for this he attacked Tariny for his offensive relationship with his mother and sister. 

 19. PW 3 Mujibur Rahman supporting the prosecution case said that his house is in the contiguous north east of the house of Tariny who used to live in his village home and also with his son at Dhaka and PW 2 and his mother used to live at the house of Tariny who returned home on the 19th Falgoon, 1385 BS and he PW 3 saw him (Tariny) a little before sunset on that date. He said that at about midnight Nikhil's mother went to his house and raised alarm and on his query she said that Tariny was abducted from his hut by some miscreants by force but they could not recognise the miscreants. He then went to the house of Tariny and did not find him there. He said that Umed Ali Master PW 6 and many others came to the house of Tariny after the miscreants left the house and searched for Tariny but they could not find him. He said that subsequently he came to know that the dead body of Tariny was recovered from the river. He admitted that they purchased three kanis of land from Mohananda Singha and his co-sharers and built house there. He said that Sorojuni was aged about 30/31 years and she was beautiful to look at. He admitted that he did not state to police that he saw the deceased in the evening. 

 21. The above PWs said that on the night of occurrence, they went to the house of Tariny on hearing hue and cry and came to learn from Nikhil, his mother and sister that Tariny was abducted by unknown miscreants. The above witnesses have got no enmity with the accused appellants and no material contradictions transpire in their evidence during cross-examination. These witnesses said that they searched Tariny on the night of the occurrence but could not trace him out. 

 26. From the above evidence, it is clear that the deceased Tariny was abducted from his house on the night following 19th Falgoon, 1385 BS corresponding to 4.3.79 about 11/11-30 PM and his dead body was recovered from a doba of Brahmaputra river near the village Chartaki on 8.3.79, in the manner said by the PWs as stated above. We do not find any reason to disbelieve the prosecution case regarding the abduction and recovery of the dead body of Tariny in the manner stated above. 

 28. It is not denied that accused Abdul Ali and Abdul Bari purchased a portion of a homestead of Tariny from his co-sharers and Tariny filed a pre-emption case against them being pre-emption Misc. Case No. 8 of 1975 in the Court of the Munsif, Sadar Mymensingh and pre-emption and his prayer for taking delivery of possession was pending during his life time and possession was delivered after the .occurrence, as appears from Exts. 6 and 7. 

 30. Mr. MA Malek, the learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that the evidence of an approver is to be accepted very cautiously as provided under section 114 illustration (b) of the Evidence Act. He submits that in the present case, the evidence of PW 2 is not corroborated by any reliable or independent witness and, as such, the conviction cannot be sustained, basing solely on the evidence of PW 2. In support of his contention he referred to and relied on the decision made in the cases of Ibrahim Bhak and another Vs. Crown reported in 7 DLR (FC) 123 and Rafiq Ahmed Vs. State reported in 11 DLR 91. In the case reported in 11 DLR 91 it was, inter alia observed as follows: 

 The discussion and decision made in the case reported in 7 DLR is not very much relevant and not applicable in the facts of the present case. Under section 133 of the Evidence Act an accomplice is a competent witness against an accused person; and a conviction may be sustained on his evidence. Section 133 runs as follows: 

 "114. The court may presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, regard being had to the common course of natural events, human conduct and public and private business, in their relation to the facts of the particular case. 

 In the present case, let us see whether the statements of PW 2 made in court and the confessional statement Ext. 17 proved in court both by PW 2 and PW 11 Mr. GM Ahmed who recorded the confessional statement are corroborated in material particulars. 

 33. PW 15 Md. Hamidul Islam, the finger print expert and PW 15 Mr. AK Mozammel Hossain, the hand writing expert on examination of the alleged signatures and finger prints of deceased Tariny Kanta Singha in the kabala Ext. 9 and the relevant register maintained by the Sub-Registrar Ext. 21, found that the alleged thumb impressions and signatures of deceased Tariny are forged. PW 36 Sk. Abdul Basher, cm Inspector and Investigating Officer of the case stated that he seized the above forged documents and filed a case against the offenders and on investigation by himself, submitted charge sheet against the offenders and Session Case No. 250/81 arising out of that case, was pending at the time he deposed. The letter of PW 2 Ext. 4 appears to have referred to the kabala Ext. 9. 

 36. The above oral and documentary evidence namely Exts. 1, 2, 3, 4, 9 and 15 corroborate the statements of PW 2 made in the confessional statement Ext. 17 and in court in all material particulars. In other words, the requirements of section 114 Illustration (b) of the Evidence Act is fully complied with in the present case. 

 37. It is suggested by the defence that the deceased used to enjoy both the mother and sister of PW 2 and for this PW 2 was aggrieved with the deceased who might be killed by some other persons, as he was a man of bad character. It may be that as the deceased was a widower for the last 20/22 years and the mother of PW 2 was a young widow, they might have immoral relationship privately and even assuming that the deceased used to enjoy the mother and sister of PW 2, in that case also, the position of the defence case is not improved. Rather, it supports the prosecution case that PW 2 and his mother became alienated and also hostile to the deceased, as the deceased was not repaying the money and was not giving the land as promised. He might have offended PW 2 for his immoral relationship with his mother and sister and for this, it was quite natural that PW 2 consented to cooperate with the accused persons to remove the deceased from the earth and this factor also support the prosecution case. 

 39. Mr. MA Malek, the learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that the case of some of the accused persons acquitted by the learned Judge is similar and stand on same footing with the case of the appellants and, as such, the learned Additional Sessions Judge was not justified in convicting the appellants while he acquitted the co-accuseds on the same evidence. 

 40. It is no doubt true that the evidence against some of the acquitted co-accused`s is similar to the evidence against the appellants and, as such, the case of both the appellants and some of the acquitted co-accused`s stand on the same footing. But the acquittal of the co-accused whose case stands on the same footing with that of the appellants, cannot be ground for their acquittal also in the appeal when there is sufficient evidence on record, as discussed above, justifying their conviction. 

 41. Mr. MA Malek, the learned Advocate for the appellants, however could not cite any case decision to support his contention. We were therefore, unable to accept the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants that the appeal should be allowed and the appellants should be acquitted as some of the co-accused`s are acquitted having the same evidence against them also as a sound principle of law.
